title: BYORP Tutorial Test
bodyHtml:
1. See how it works

(Add diagram here)


HuGeAMP+KPN: Research Portal is Build Your Own Research Portal (BYORP) service with which researchers can build research portals by themselves. We also provide Knowledge Portal on Demand service for portal projects that require customized visualizers, data display/filtering tools and own visual representations of the projects.  (example: http://lipiddroplet.org)

Hugeampkpn.org
Hugeampkpn.org is where your research portal will be shared. A research portal pages you create on hugeampkpncms.org can be accessed on hugeampkpn.org with your unique page id. (example: http://hugeampkpn.org/research.html?pageid=demo)

Hugeampkpncms.org
Hugeampkpncms.org is where you build your own research portals. It is a CMS (Content Management System) built for 1) uploading your research data, 2) configuring displays of the data, and 3) building portals with the display pages. In the following sections, BYORP step will be explained with demos.

2. Create your account
(How do we want handle the users?)

3. User privilege

Authenticated users and Registered users share same privileges except the storage space. Authenticated users have 20MB(?) of storage space. Registered users have unlimited storage space. To upgrade your account to registered user one, please contact portal team. (contact page)

4. JSON objects and arrays

If you are already familiar with JSON objects and arrays, you can skip to the next. On hugeampkpncms.org, configuring research pages is done with using JSON objects and arrays. JSON objects are a type of data that can contain information blocks tied in key to value relations. Here is an example of JSON object.

{ "fruit 1":"Apple", "fruit 2":"Banana", "fruit 3":"Mango"}

Each pieces of informations are separated by commas. Please keep in mind that the last item in JSON objects don't have following comma. Having a comma after the last item in a JSON object will be taken as an error and break rendering process in hugeampken.org, display of your research page. 

Arrays are list of information pieces wrapped with brackets ([]). Here is an example.

["Apple", "Banana", "Mango"]

Again, the last items in arrays don't have following commas. 

You can learn more about JSON objects and arrays here. (https://medium.com/@angela.amarapala/difference-between-arrays-and-json-objects-fa1c8598f9f1)

5. Upload your data

You created an account on hugeampkpncms.org and got an approval email from us. Now you want to create a research page. To do that, unless you want to create pages with no data, you need to upload data files (Also, diagram images and pdf files for downloading) to display on your research pages. 
Clicking Manage Your Files menu will switch the browser window to file browser with your space open. 

(screen capture of file browser here)

Click Upload menu. Then click Add files button. Now you can choose the data files to upload. Uploader will upload the files to your space.

Important!!!!
Data file
Research Portal takes only .csv file format for data. It is set this way to minimize loading time and maximize the scale of the data. Each file can be up to 8MB but, not recommended going over 6MB. Data conversion to renderable format happens on browser side in real time. Bigger the file size will take longer to display. Also, consumes more resource (cpu power and memory) of viewers computers which may cause slow sorting and filtering of data. Well formatted data looks like the following.

CHR,POS,REF,ALT,RSID,PVAL
1,721290,G,C,rs12565286,3.8345e-02
1,976963,A,G,rs150359724,4.3785e-03
1,1120431,G,A,rs1320571,2.3373e-02

Other file types
You can also upload images and document files to compose your research pages. Hugeampkpncms takes jpg, png and gif files for images and pdf and docx files for documents.

File names
Please don't use special characters, hyphens and spaces in file names. Here is a example of a good file name:
"project_name_data_name_version_number.csv"

Same logic applies for image files and document files.

6. Build your first research page

Let's create your first research page. Click Add page menu. Then click Research page menu. It will open a page with full of input fields. For your first research page, you need to fill only few fields. 
1. Give a page title. It will appear in title section of your research page.
2. Give a page ID. Page ID has to be unique. If your page id happens to be identical to someone else's, one of them will be ignored and fails to be displayed. How you can make your page id will be explained in the following section. 
3. Give a file name you uploaded in Data Points field. Adding multiple files to a research page will be explained in the following section.
4. Close to the bottom of the page, you will find Page mode option. Set it to public.
5. Save.

Now, go to hugeampkpn.org and put your page id in the following format in the url box. 
"https://hugeampkpn.org/research.html?pageid=your_page_id"
You will see your data displayed on the page. You just created your first research page.

In the following section, each fields in the configuration form will be discussed.

7. Fields in configuration form

Title
Title of your research page

Page ID
Unique id to query the content of a configuration form from hugeampkpn.org. You can make your page id absolutely unique by adding the id of a configuration form. Fill out title and temporary page id, and save the form. You will see the url changes to hugeampkpncms.org/node/number. The number after "node/" is the id of the configuration form. Open the form in edit mode. Put the number at the end of the page id. Here is a good example. "biomarker_eqtl_10"

Is Project Landing Page
If the research page you configure is a project landing page. Research pages come with "Research Method" tab as default. If your intention is to create a page with static information such as project overview, check this option.

Data Points
Data points can be the files you uploaded to your account on hugeampkpncms.org or files on remote places or apis. As long as they return data in csv format, it will work fine. 
A research page can have single data point or multiple data points. In case of multiple data points, separate each data points with comma. Here is an example.
"file1.csv, file2.csv, file3.csv"
If there are more than one data points, a drop down menu to select data point will appear on the research page. 

Data Points List Labels
You have multiple data points, and you want to make the labels on the Select Data drop down more human readable, you can set that here. Here is an example.
{
"file1.csv":"File 1 label",
"file2.csv":"File 2 label",
"file3.csv":"File 3 label"
}

Data Table Format
First please take a look at this example page. (URL to example page) You can find that the data table has two levels of structure, top level rows and sub tables you can open with evidence button. You can build this two leveled table in this field. Let's say you have 10 columns your data. First 5 columns are for the top level rows, and the last 5 columns will be used to build sub tables. 
Data:
col 1,col 2,col 3,col 4,col 5,col 6,col 7,col 8,col 9,col 10
value 1-1, value 1-2, ​​​​​​​value 1-3, ​​​​​​​value 1-4, ​​​​​​​value 1-5, ​​​​​​​value 1-6, ​​​​​​​value 1-7, ​​​​​​​value 1-8, ​​​​​​​value 1-9, ​​​​​​​value 1-10 
value 2-1, ​​​​​​​value 2-2, ​​​​​​​value 2-3, ​​​​​​​value 2-4, ​​​​​​​value 2-5, ​​​​​​​value 2-6, ​​​​​​​value 2-7, ​​​​​​​value 2-8, ​​​​​​​value 2-9, ​​​​​​​value 2-10

Formatting:
{
"top rows":["col 1", "col 2", "col 3", "col 4", "col 5"],
"features":["feature 1","feature 2"],
"feature 1":["col 6","col 7"],
"feature 2":["col 8","col 9","col 10"]
}

And here is how the table looks like:
(Screen capture of the table)

Converting data
You can create new columns from raw data. Let's say you have this data:

CHR,POS,REF,ALT,RSID,PVAL
1,721290,G,C,rs12565286,3.8345e-02
1,976963,A,G,rs150359724,4.3785e-03
1,1120431,G,A,rs1320571,2.3373e-02

And you want to 1) join CHR and POS to create Locus column, 2) join REF and ALT to create Allele column and 3) add -Log10(P-value) column to render Manhattan plot. Here is how you do it.
{
"data convert":[
{"type":"join","field name":"Locus","fields to join":["CHR","POS"],"join by":":"},
{"type":"join","field name":"Allele","fields to join":["REF","ALT"],"join by":"/"},
{"type":"raw","field name":"rsID","raw field":"RSID"},
{"type":"raw","field name":"P-Value","raw field":"PVAL"},
{"type":"calculate","field name":"-log10(P-Value)","raw field":"PVAL","calculation type":"-log10"}
],
"top rows":["Locus","Allele","SNP","P-Value"]
}
